_comment: Project permissions for the `claude -p` brain invoked by runlib/brain_io.py.
THREAT MODEL: the brain reads a context bundle containing UNSANITIZED external
text - news headlines, SEC filing prose (up to 10k chars of MD&A), 8-K bodies.
It is granted Read/Glob/Grep plus WebSearch/WebFetch. An adversarial string in
any of that text is instruction-shaped input sitting inside a file the brain is
told to open. The validator cannot see this: it only inspects parsed proposals,
PRIMARY CONTROL is not these rules - it is that secrets now live OUTSIDE the
working directory (see tools/envload.py). Glob and Grep are cwd-scoped, and Grep
PRINTS MATCHING LINES, so a Read-only deny rule would never have stopped
`grep ALPACA`. Relocation closes that; these rules are defense in depth for any
NO WEBFETCH DOMAIN ALLOWLIST, deliberately. CLAUDE.md makes WebSearch mandatory
before every BUY and the brain WebFetches filings and news to verify catalysts;
pinning it to a host list would break the research the strategy depends on. With
credentials out of the working directory the residual egress risk is bundle
content, not secrets - a much lower severity. Revisit if secrets ever need to sit
